title: Mentor Recruiting Influence Graph
placeholder: Click any channel for its population estimate and whether the club currently reaches it.

nodes.label: Club Outreach
detail: Everywhere the club currently announces itself. Two channels, both of which reach people who are already inside the school community.
Both existing channels draw from the same population. Doubling the effort on either one reaches more of the people the club already reaches.
Which single new edge would reach the most people the club has never spoken to?

nodes.label:
PTA Email
List
detail: About 180 families, all with a child already at the school.
Connected. This is where most current mentors came from.
Everyone here is already a school parent. It is an excellent channel and it cannot reach anybody outside that set.

nodes.label:
Library
Bulletin Board
detail: Perhaps 60 people a week who read the board, heavily overlapping the PTA list.
Connected. Free, passive, and low effort.
A notice board reaches whoever walks past. It cannot be aimed, and it produces enquiries rather than mentors.

nodes.label:
Neighbourhood
Congregation
detail: About 200 adults, most of them not school parents.
A relationship, not a poster. Attend something first -- an ask from a stranger to a congregation is the one that fails.
Broad population, few of whom have a technical background. Good for volunteer mentors, not for professionals.

nodes.label:
Boys & Girls
Club Programme
detail: About 120 families, with substantial overlap into households the school outreach misses.
A staff contact and a conversation about whether your club serves the same students or competes with them.
This is a student channel more than a mentor channel -- worth knowing which problem you are solving before you spend the effort.

nodes.label:
Women Who
Code Meetup
detail: About 300 members, almost none of them currently connected to the club.
Not reached. The largest untapped population on this graph.
Why it is the highest-leverage node
Largest untapped population AND a single plausible point of contact -- a meetup organiser who can put one message in front of all 300. Most channels have one of those two properties. This has both.
Technical people who chose to spend evenings on it. This is where professional mentors come from, and it is the gap in most clubs' mentor mix.

nodes.label:
Local Engineering
Employer
detail: About 250 staff, reachable in principle through an internal channel.
A named internal sponsor. Without one, an approach to a company reaches a mailbox nobody owns.
Strong technical pool, and the slowest of the four to convert -- volunteering competes with a demanding job.

legend.text: A dashed edge is a connection that does not exist yet

spotlight.heading: Women Who Code Meetup
detail: It is the only channel on the map with both properties that matter: the largest untapped population (about 300) AND a single plausible point of contact who can put one message in front of all of them.
The congregation and the employer need a relationship built first. The Boys & Girls Club reaches students rather than mentors. Each is worth doing; none is the first call.
Reach is not the same as size. A channel of 300 you cannot address is worth less than a channel of 120 you can.
